title: Golden case
description: Plan section 21.2 (schema; the early variants; full 15-case set + RG-01..07). Amended at mode/source_id/pii_status/allowed_trajectories/allowed_tools/forbidden_tools/rubric added.

scenario.description: One-line description of what this case exercises.

gd_ref.description: Cross-reference into the plan's GD-01..15 / RG-01..07 numbering, where applicable.

fixture_id.description: References an entry in datasets/fixtures/manifest.json, never an inline payload — one source of truth for fixture data.

expected_outcome.description: Domain-level expected result (e.g. gap value, blocker codes, receipt shape) — re-derived against a live/measured artifact, never carried forward from an assumption (agentic-tdd-and-gate: 're-derive expected-call and expected-output fixtures against a live probe').

budgets.description: Per-case budget overrides (plan section 6.3's defaults apply when omitted): agent cycles, MCP attempts, token ceiling, active-execution seconds.

mode.description: which harness runs this case. `replay` goes through the real compiled graph via graph/replay.py; `fake_backend` uses tests/support/write_backend.py. The runner dispatches on this field, never infers it.

source_id.description: provenance of this case's data -- a live-recording id, a seeded-generator run id, or a hand-authored label. Distinct from `gd_ref`, which cross-references plan numbering, not data origin.

pii_status.description: whether this case's input carries pseudonymised live data (sanitized), generated data with no real-guest origin (synthetic), or carries no PII-bearing fields at all (none).

allowed_trajectories.description: the set of node-name sequences this case accepts as a correct path through the graph. Feeds TrajectoryAdherence (plan section 13.3), which is a distance to the NEAREST allowed trajectory -- omitted when a case has no trajectory expectation (e.g. a fake_backend safety case).

allowed_tools.description: MCP tool names this case's trajectory may call. Omitted when not meaningful for the case.

forbidden_tools.description: MCP tool names this case's trajectory must never call -- e.g. the remove tool on an ordinary add-path case. Omitted when not meaningful for the case.

rubric.description: one-line pass criterion in prose, for cases whose correctness is not fully captured by expected_outcome's structural equality (e.g. an RG fault-injection case's rubric).
